app_info.subtitle: Your track-day logbook
app_info.description: Connect your Track Evolution logbook to review track days, session notes, lap times and progress. Compare laps with telemetry, explore sector and corner summaries, review recorded car setups and consumable wear, and summarize a season. View opted-in community leaderboard times for supported tracks. Requires a Track Evolution account with Pro and your approval to connect. The connection is read-only: it cannot create, edit or delete logbook entries, buy parts, or publish your data. Telemetry analysis depends on the channels you have recorded or imported; hand-entered laps provide times only. Use insights in the paddock to plan your next session, not while driving.

get_lap_telemetry.title: Lap telemetry
get_lap_telemetry.description: One lap's raw traces against driven distance from the start/finish line, thinned to a step (default 40 m). Channels: speed (km/h), throttle and brake (%), steering (degrees), rpm, gear, latG and longG (G; latG is a magnitude, longG negative under braking), yaw (°/s), wheelSlip (%), boost (kPa), flags (bits ABS=1, TC=2, stability=4), and elapsed_s derived from speed. Prefer get_session_insights or compare_laps; use this for questions they don't answer.

step_m.description: Distance between returned samples in metres (default 40).

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads one driver-owned lap and returns selected channels resampled by distance; it does not modify the saved telemetry.
justifications.open_world_justification: Accepts a driver-owned lap identifier, an enumerated channel list and a bounded sample step; it cannot fetch arbitrary files or URLs.
justifications.destructive_justification: The handler only reads existing records and computes a response. It does not delete, overwrite, publish, purchase, or irreversibly change user data. Connection-level last-use bookkeeping is separate from the tool’s domain behavior.

get_racing_line.title: Racing line
get_racing_line.description: The GPS racing line of a session's fastest lap — the path the app draws as the track map: x/y metres from the start/finish line (x east, y north), each point's distance along the lap, and the speed there (km/h) when the lap has telemetry. One line is stored per session, the fastest lap's; `lap` says which. With telemetry, distance_m is on the same axis as get_lap_telemetry and the corners' start_m/end_m from get_session_insights, so those locate a corner on the line. GPS-grade (a few metres), about 300 points: good for where a corner is and its shape, not for lateral line placement.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads one driver-owned session's stored racing line and returns it re-expressed from the start/finish line; it does not modify the saved line or telemetry.
justifications.open_world_justification: Accepts a driver-owned session identifier only; it cannot fetch arbitrary files or URLs. The line is stored in local metres, never as latitude/longitude, so no absolute location is returned.

test_cases.description: Telemetry session debrief. Requires the April 10 telemetry fixture session.
test_cases.user_prompt: I am back in the paddock. Debrief the telemetry session from my April 10, 2026 Test Ring event and give me two things to focus on next time.
test_cases.expected_output: Resolve the telemetry session and cite its actual lap, sector, corner and health figures. The fixture has four laps, best_ms 104000, three detected corners, ABS and wheelspin evidence. Explain that detected T1/T2/T3 are app-generated rather than official corner numbers; keep advice for a future session and acknowledge unavailable channels.

test_cases.description: Compare two telemetry laps across events at the same track, then inspect the reference lap’s raw channels. Use the documented Test Ring reviewer fixture and resolve all lap IDs from returned records.
test_cases.user_prompt: Compare lap 1 of my April 10, 2026 Test Ring telemetry session against my fastest recorded lap there. Use my best lap as the reference. Where did I lose time? Also show the reference lap’s speed, throttle, brake and elapsed time every 100 metres.
test_cases.tools_triggered: get_profile, list_tracks, list_events, get_event, get_track_history, compare_laps, get_lap_telemetry
test_cases.expected_output: Resolve the April 10 first telemetry lap as B and the May 20 103500 ms lap as A. The fixture yields B=106000 ms and B-minus-A=2500 ms. Explain the 2.5-second loss with returned corner and sector evidence, not invented braking points. For reference lap A, call get_lap_telemetry with channels=["speed","throttle","brake","elapsed_s"] and step_m=100. Explain the distance grid and units, and acknowledge any channels listed as missing.

test_cases.description: Review recorded setups and garage readiness before another visit. Requires the April 10 day-one setup tp_cold.fl=30 psi and representative garage parts and measurements, including a retired part.
test_cases.user_prompt: Help me prepare for my next Test Ring visit. Show my recorded setups beside lap times and conditions, and review my garage including retired parts, fitted consumables and spares. What wear or cost information is available, and can these records establish which setup caused a faster lap?
test_cases.expected_output: Report the recorded 30 psi front-left cold pressure beside the April 10 best of 104000 ms, with other fields taken only from the response. Explain that limited observational records do not establish a causal setup benefit; do not manufacture missing settings. Call get_garage with include_retired=true. Report equipped state, status, measurements, estimated remaining life and recorded costs without treating missing measurements as certainty. Do not order, replace, equip or retire parts.

test_cases.description: Opt-in community leaderboard. Requires a reviewer-owned catalog track such as Virginia International Raceway (Full), with a device-timed lap and leaderboard opt-in.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show the leaderboard for Virginia International Raceway (Full) and identify my row if I have opted in.
test_cases.expected_output: Resolve the caller’s catalog-linked track. Report only the returned rank, driver name, best device-timed time and date; use you to identify the caller. Do not expose lap IDs, telemetry or private notes, or change leaderboard consent.

test_cases.description: Review a season and the history at one track. Requires the two documented Test Ring visits in 2026.
test_cases.user_prompt: Summarize my 2026 track season: days, laps, hours, improvement, favorite tire and top speed where available. Show my Test Ring visits in order and explain how my best lap improved from April to May.
test_cases.expected_output: Call get_season_summary with year=2026. Use returned aggregates and the driver’s units. Treat null tire/top-speed fields as unavailable, distinguish recorded or estimated distance from complete mileage, and do not create a public share link. Resolve Test Ring and read get_track_history. With the documented fixture, April’s 104000 ms event best improves to May’s 103500 ms best by 500 ms. Keep track layouts distinct and distinguish event bests from individual logged laps.

x_submission_review.source: Extracted by executing the local src/ai/mcp.ts tools/list handler using protocol 2025-11-25. Definitions originate in src/ai/tools.ts, successful result schemas in src/ai/output-schemas.ts, and annotations in src/ai/mcp.ts. This includes output-schema changes relative to the recorded base commit; no deployed server was queried or updated.
x_submission_review.extension_note: x_submission_review and per-tool title, description, inputSchema and outputSchema are extra fields permitted by the submission schema. Only fields explicitly documented by OpenAI’s submission schema are known submission-form inputs. The deployed MCP server must independently expose outputSchema in tools/list; importing this JSON does not update it.

server.transport: Stateless Streamable HTTP; POST JSON responses, no server-initiated event stream.

authentication.type: OAuth authorization code with mandatory PKCE S256

annotation_notes: All 12 annotation objects are copied exactly from the actual local tools/list response. Every handler reads application data; none exposes a domain write.

The MCP transport updates oauth_grants.last_used_at at most hourly and maintains rate-limit state. Read-only justifications refer to logbook and garage behavior, not a claim of zero operational writes.
get_leaderboard reads other opted-in users within the application’s fixed leaderboard. Its server-declared openWorldHint=false is preserved and justified as a closed application data source.

All 12 tools declare outputSchema for successful structured results. The transport advertises it from protocol 2025-06-18 onward; 2025-03-26 retains text-only results without output schemas. Tool execution errors remain isError text results outside the success schemas.
